solve:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Performs a 0-1 BFS on a grid, using precomputed obstacle-limited maximum travel distances in the four cardinal directions, to find and print the minimum number of direction choices needed to reach the target, or -1 if it is unreachable." solve]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Read the first line of standard input and unpack the three integers h, w, k using LI(). RESULT h, w, k]
            [COMMAND Read the second line of standard input and unpack the four integers y, x, s, t using LI(). RESULT y, x, s, t]
            [COMMAND Assign D = [(k, 0), (-k, 0), (0, k), (0, -k)]. RESULT D]
            [COMMAND Subtract 1 from each of y, x, s, and t to convert them to 0-based coordinates. RESULT y, x, s, t]
            [COMMAND Initialize q as a deque containing the single initial state (y, x, -1, 0). RESULT q]
            [COMMAND Initialize d as an h by w grid filled with float('inf'), then set d[y][x] = 0. RESULT d]
            [COMMAND Initialize ri, le, do, up, and c as empty lists. RESULT ri, le, do, up, c]
            [COMMAND For each row index i from 0 to h-1, read the next input row and append it to c, then append a list of w zeros to each of ri, le, do, and up. RESULT c, ri, le, do, up]
            [COMMAND For each row i from 0 to h-1, set ri[i][w-1] = 0; then for j from w-2 down to 0, set ri[i][j] = 0 if c[i][j+1] == '@', otherwise set ri[i][j] = min(k, ri[i][j+1] + 1). RESULT ri]
            [COMMAND For each row i from 0 to h-1, set le[i][0] = 0; then for j from 1 to w-1, set le[i][j] = 0 if c[i][j-1] == '@', otherwise set le[i][j] = min(k, le[i][j-1] + 1). RESULT le]
            [COMMAND For each column j from 0 to w-1, set do[h-1][j] = 0; then for i from h-2 down to 0, set do[i][j] = 0 if c[i+1][j] == '@', otherwise set do[i][j] = min(k, do[i+1][j] + 1). RESULT do]
            [COMMAND For each column j from 0 to w-1, set up[0][j] = 0; then for i from 1 to h-1, set up[i][j] = 0 if c[i-1][j] == '@', otherwise set up[i][j] = min(k, up[i-1][j] + 1). RESULT up]
            [COMMAND While q is not empty, pop the leftmost state into y, x, p, l. If (y, x) equals (s, t), print d[s][t] and return immediately. RESULT stdout]
            [COMMAND Within the while q loop, for the popped state, set nd = d[y][x] + 1. RESULT nd]
            [COMMAND Within the while q loop, for i in 0..3, select the movement vector: i=0 -> (-up[y][x], 0), i=1 -> (do[y][x], 0), i=2 -> (0, -le[y][x]), i=3 -> (0, ri[y][x]); then compute ny = y + dy and nx = x + dx. RESULT ny, nx, dy, dx]
            [COMMAND Within the for i in 0..3 loop, if (ny, nx) equals (y, x), skip this direction using continue. RESULT none]
            [COMMAND Within the for i in 0..3 loop, if nd < d[ny][nx], set d[ny][nx] = nd, compute diff = abs(ny - y) + abs(nx - x), and append (ny, nx, i, diff) to q. RESULT q, d]
            [COMMAND Within the while q loop, after the four-direction for loop, if p >= 0 and l > 1, set dy and dx from the direction table dd[p], then compute ny = y + dy and nx = x + dx. RESULT ny, nx, dy, dx]
            [COMMAND Within the zero-cost continuation branch, set nd = d[y][x]; if nd < d[ny][nx], set d[ny][nx] = nd and appendleft (ny, nx, p, l - 1) to q. RESULT q, d]
            [COMMAND After the while loop exits because q is empty, print -1 and return. RESULT stdout]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
